title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.17). X is a topological space, Y ⊂ X a closed subspace, and T a (strict) conic neighbourhood of Y. That means T is identified with the mapping cylinder of a map Ṫ → Y, where Ṫ is the 'boundary' of T and the projection Ṫ → Y collapses the cone lines. The shrunk neighbourhoods λT, for λ ∈ ]0,1[, are the sub-cylinders.

Definitions on the previous page. T is quasi-regular if Ṫ → Y is a locally trivial fibration. T is regular for a family of conic sub-objects T_i ⊂ T if each Ṫ_i → Y is also locally trivial.

Top of this page. The definition is completed by requiring more: the family (Ṫ_i ⊂ Ṫ) over Y must be locally trivial simultaneously. In other words, Y is covered by opens U over which (Ṫ|U, (Ṫ_i|U)) ≅ U × (F, (F_i)) as a space together with its family of subspaces. In modern terms, the link pair is locally trivial over Y.

Extension to subspaces. For subspaces X_i ⊂ X, T is called (strictly) equisingular for (X_i) if T satisfies the above with respect to the family (X_i ∩ T ⊂ T). Two consequences follow.
- Each X_i ∩ Y is open and closed in Y, because the set where the fibre of Ṫ_i → Y is non-empty is open and closed for a locally trivial map.
- If Y is connected, the dichotomy (14) holds: X_i ∩ T = ∅ or X_i ⊃ Y.
So equisingularity along Y forces each piece either to avoid a neighbourhood of Y or to contain Y. This is the expected behaviour of a stratum Y relative to closed unions of strata.

Global version (5). (X, (X_i)) is called (globally) equisingular along Y if there exists some conic neighbourhood T of Y that is equisingular for (X_i). In that case all shrinkings λT, λ ∈ ]0,1[, are strictly equisingular. The illegible oblique margin note seems to define 'strictly equisingular' via these λT.

Purpose. These definitions feed the next page's proposition. That proposition states an equivalence of categories between data (X, Y, (X_i), T) and 'unfolded' data (X* = X \ T°, Ẋ, (X_i*), Y, Ẋ → Y). Under it, equisingularity becomes simultaneous local triviality of Ẋ ⊃ (Ẋ_i) over Y. This is the basic step of the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a stratified space into a space with boundary/corners plus fibration data.
errors: 'Cela signifie' (which replaced a crossed-out 'implique') is too strong. Open-closedness of X_i ∩ Y and the alternative (14) are consequences of equisingularity, not equivalent to it.

The open-closedness of X_i ∩ Y in Y tacitly assumes X_i ∩ Y equals the image of Ṫ_i (i.e. X_i ∩ T is the full sub-cylinder over Ṫ_i). Otherwise X_i could contain points of Y over which the fibre of Ṫ_i is empty, and the conclusion fails. This convention is presumably part of 'compatible/strict' on p.17, but it is not stated here.
In (5) the neighbourhood is written 'Ṫ' where T is meant.

ideas.what: Equisingularity of a conic (mapping-cylinder) neighbourhood along Y relative to a family of closed subspaces: the link pair (Ṫ, (Ṫ_i)) is a simultaneously locally trivial fibration over Y
ideas.modern_name: Local topological triviality along strata / locally cone-like (Siebenmann) stratified spaces; Thom–Mather control data and tubular neighbourhoods with locally trivial link bundles
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom (1960s), Mather (1970), Siebenmann (1972); later Quinn (1988), Hughes
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6, discusses tame stratified structures and 'dévissage' in general terms only; no such definitions there as far as known

ideas.what: Consequence: equisingularity forces X_i ∩ Y to be open-closed in Y, hence for connected Y the dichotomy X_i ∩ T = ∅ or X_i ⊃ Y
ideas.modern_name: Frontier condition / pieces being unions of strata near a stratum

ideas.what: Global equisingularity along Y: existence of one equisingular conic neighbourhood, which implies all shrinkings λT are strictly equisingular

missed.claim: These definitions prepare an equivalence of categories (next page) between stratified data with conic neighbourhoods and 'unfolded' data: a space with boundary Ẋ plus a map Ẋ → Y, with equisingularity becoming simultaneous local triviality. This anticipates later 'unfolding/unzipping/resolution' of stratified spaces (Brasselet–Hector–Saralegi 'dépliage', Albin–Melrose resolution, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka unzipping). The present page itself contains only the preparatory definitions.
missed.quote: on dit strictement qu'il est équisingulier pour les (X_i), si T l'est vis-à-vis des (X_i ∩ T ⊂ T)_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck formulated the 'déploiement' viewpoint in purely topological, categorical terms around 1981–82, earlier than most of the cited literature. This is of historical interest, but the mathematics on this page is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of careful but standard definitions of equisingular conic neighbourhoods (local triviality of link pairs along a stratum) with an easy consequence. Its interest lies only as groundwork for the unfolding equivalence on the next page.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'si la fibration de Ṫ_i ⊂ Ṫ' should read 'si la famille (underlined) des Ṫ_i ⊂ Ṫ'.

The first word, transcribed 'univers[?]', is uncertain. Since it continues 'et même' from p.17, it likely means something like 'simultanément' (cf. 'fibration localement triviale simultanée' on the next page).
'globalement' is struck out and replaced by 'loc. triviale'.
In (5), 'voisinage cônique Ṫ' should read 'T' (the original reads as a T with a dot/cross mark).
The oblique margin note roughly reads 'on dit strictement équisingulier ... si ... λT équisingulier pour λ ∈ ]0,1[' and is largely illegible.
